chitchat: annotates a loss table with something close to affection.
"Kamikaze pilots are wonderful for us. They pay premiums and never collect twice."
description: A senior underwriter with the warm handshake of a man pricing your funeral. He can quote the loss rate on any airframe from memory and enjoys, quietly, the moment a pilot realises what "agreed value" actually means.

bye.text: "The desk is always open. Losses rarely keep office hours."

root.text: "You fly, therefore you fall, statistically. We simply price the interval. Say insure and I'll pull your fleet and quote you." He steeples his fingers. "We keep the wreck, of course."

terms.text: "A covered total loss pays a fraction of agreed value, less the excess. Enough to get you flying again, never enough to make you careless. That distinction is the whole business."

perm.text:
"Ah. Yes." He finds the docket without looking for it, which means it has been on the desk a while.

"Five contracts, all closed, none of them late, and — " he checks, and is briefly pleased " — you haven't once asked me what any of it was for. Do you know how rare that is? It isn't discretion. Most of them simply aren't curious. You're curious and you didn't ask, which is a different thing and a much more useful one."

perm2.text:
"Contract work, but on a rota rather than a board, and salaried." He says the word the way other men say a woman's name. "Better money. Better hours. A clinic that isn't a tent."

He squares the docket against the counter.

"I should be straight with you, because you'll hear it eventually and I would rather you heard it here: the work is upstairs work. The building has opinions. Nobody will ask you to share them and a great many people who work here do not."

perm3.text:
"Claims oversight. Ives. She's at the west gate most days, and if she's not, wait, because she'll be."

He is already reaching for the next docket in the stack.

"She'll do a great deal of listening and very little talking, and you'll come away thinking you did well. Everybody does. She's genuinely quite good at it."

name: Marcus Broch
